title: Compact mode: resolve placeholder collisions, migrate legacy tokens, and spec adaptive assistive layout for rich inputs
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: In compact density and compact mode, multiline fields, numeric inputs with prefix/suffix affordances, and fields that receive browser autofill frequently exhibit visual collisions: placeholders overlap with affixes or floating labels, assistive help text overlaps validation chips, and legacy spacing tokens produce inconsistent hit areas. This causes fragile CSS workarounds in product apps, increases visual regressions during token updates, and creates accessibility issues for screen-reader focus order and error announcements.

Objective: Define a single coherent spec and migration path that: (1) resolves placeholder/floating-label and affix collisions in compact mode across single-line, multiline and numeric inputs; (2) provides a clear legacy -> new token mapping and migration steps for engineering; (3) prescribes assistive layout rules so help text, character counters, and validation errors never overlap and maintain logical DOM order for screen readers; (4) gives an engineering-friendly set of acceptance tests and visual regression snapshots for automation.

Constraints and considerations: must preserve keyboard/IME behavior for international input, avoid large increases to vertical rhythm in compact contexts, keep hit targets within accessibility guidelines where possible, and support autofill flows (Chrome, Safari) without content flicker. Work must coordinate with ENG for runtime token overrides and with PM for rollout timing to reduce product regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with exact spacing tokens and visual examples for single-line, multiline, and numeric fields in compact mode is reviewed and approved by Eng and Accessibility
Legacy token mapping table provided (legacy token -> new token name), and a migration checklist for front-end teams is published
Figma component variants covering: default, focused, filled, autofill, error, help-text-expanded, counter, prefix/suffix present are included and annotated
Automated visual regression targets (Percy/Chromatic) identified and test snapshots saved for desktop and mobile breakpoints
Accessibility checklist completed: DOM order preserved, aria-describedby targets stable when assistive text toggles, screen reader walkthrough documented
design_decisions: Adopt 2-tier vertical spacing in compact mode: compact-padding-xs for inline affixes, compact-padding-sm for line-wrapped helpers
Use persistent but visually subtle prefix/suffix spacing token rather than absolute positioning to avoid overlap with IME candidate windows
Floating label will collapse above the input when autofill occurs; placeholder should be hidden once input has value to avoid collision

Help text and validation chips will occupy a single assistive row; when both exist, validation chips take precedence visually and help text moves to an "assistive overflow" state accessible via aria-expanded
Introduce new token names to avoid ambiguous legacy tokens: token-input-compact-padding, token-input-compact-affix-gap, token-assistive-row-height
tasks: Design: produce Figma component library variants and publish a concise spec (owners: Maya + Luca)
Engineering: prototype CSS variables mapping and a small JS hook to preserve DOM order for assistive text (ENG-84210)
Accessibility review: run text-to-speech walkthroughs and record any issues (owner: Alex Chen)
QA: add visual regression snapshots for 6 permutations (single/multi/numeric x empty/filled x autofill/error)
Docs: write a migration guide for frontend teams including token mapping and rollout steps
